data.name: Nenu
data.gender_notes: Nenu is used as a unisex name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: In Sanskrit, Nenu translates to 'night' or 'darkness'. In Hindu mythology, the goddess Nanda, also known as Nenu, was the foster mother of Lord Krishna. She was the embodiment of motherly love and protection. The name Nenu carries the meaning “Night, darkness” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Nenu usually hope their child will grow to embody night, darkness and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolizes the nurturing and protective aspect of a mother.
data.etymology: Nenu belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Night, darkness.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Nenu total 9, giving a life-path number of 9. Number 9 is linked with Mars and with the qualities of compassion, idealism and generosity.

data.cultural_impact: The name 'Nenu' holds cultural significance in Hindu tradition as it is associated with Nanda, the foster mother of Lord Krishna. It is a reminder of the unwavering love and nurturing care given by mothers. This name may be used as a term of endearment or as a name for a child.
data.spiritual_significance: Nenu, as the name of the foster mother of Lord Krishna, embodies the spiritual significance of unconditional love and protection. As a name, it serves as a reminder of the divine motherly love that provides solace in the darkness of life, guiding and nurturing us towards the light.
